title: Moses
lead: The prophet who led Israel out of Egypt, received the Law at Sinai, and died within sight of the promised land. Jews honor him as the greatest prophet, "whom the LORD knew face to face" (Deuteronomy 34:10); Christians also see him as a forerunner of Jesus (Hebrews 3:1–6).

sections.b: Born in Egypt under a Pharaoh who ordered Hebrew boys killed, Moses was hidden in a basket on the Nile and raised in the palace (Exodus 2). After killing an Egyptian he fled to Midian, where God spoke to him from a burning bush and revealed his name (Exodus 3). He led Israel out through the sea (Exodus 14–15), received the Ten Commandments and the covenant at Sinai (Exodus 19–24), and led the people forty years in the wilderness (Numbers). Deuteronomy presents his farewell speeches. Jewish tradition calls him Moshe Rabbenu, "Moses our teacher," and Maimonides made his unique prophecy one of the thirteen principles of Jewish faith.
sections.refs: Exodus 2–4; Exodus 14–15; Exodus 19–24; Numbers 20:1–13; Deuteronomy 34:10–12; Hebrews 3:1–6

sections.b: "There in the land of Moab, Moses the servant of the LORD died... And he buried him in the valley in the land of Moab... No one knows the place of his grave to this day" (Deuteronomy 34:5–6). The unusual burial invited later stories: Josephus says a cloud surrounded him as he vanished, and other Jewish writings told of angels and the devil at his grave. Moses appears again with Elijah at Jesus's transfiguration (Matthew 17:3).
